confidence_explanation: The timeline shows a clear progression from automated SQL injection attempts to a successful account takeover/compromise of user_07, followed by privilege escalation, massive database queries, data exfiltration via DNS and HTTPS, and finally log tampering to hide tracks.

attack_chain.description: Automated SQL injection attempts using sqlmap from IP 104.244.76.13 (evt_s86_001 to evt_s86_005).
Successful login of user_07 from the same suspicious IP (104.244.76.13), which is outside their normal IP range and normal working hours.
Privilege escalation where user_07 elevated their role to 'dba'.
Lateral movement to the production database (prod_main).
Massive database queries targeting the 'customers' table, affecting hundreds of thousands of rows (evt_s86_009 to evt_s86_011).
Data exfiltration via DNS tunneling to a known malicious domain (x7064.malicious-37.com) (evt_s86_012 to evt_s86_051).
Large scale data exfiltration via HTTPS (totaling ~161 MB) (evt_s86_052 to evt_s86_057).
Anti-forensic activity: deletion/truncation of the authentication log (/var/log/auth.log) to hide the intrusion.

gaps: Confirmation of whether the SQL injection attempts (evt_s86_001-005) were the direct mechanism used to obtain user_07's credentials.
Verification of whether user_07 was actually performing emergency maintenance (though the IP and log deletion strongly suggest otherwise).
narrative: An attacker using IP 104.244.76.13 performed SQL injection attempts before successfully logging into user_07's account. The attacker escalated privileges to DBA, queried massive amounts of customer data, exfiltrated over 160MB of data via DNS and HTTPS, and finally deleted authentication logs to cover their tracks.
